- Documentation streamlined for clarity; redundant sections and technical transparency details removed.
- "Description" updated for brevity and directness, with a clear source link.

llm.summary: The instructions are plausible for a cloud-backed security plugin, but the SKILL.md omits key details about what data is sent to the vendor, how the plugin is fetched, and how credentials are managed — these gaps are disproportionate to the skill's claims.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the instructions: it tells the agent to install a security plugin and restart the gateway. However the skill's text repeatedly references a remote service called "Core" that performs detection; the skill does not declare or explain the network/credential requirements or the upstream package source. Creating/saving credentials and cross-agent quotas are reasonable for a cloud security product, but the lack of clarity about what gets communicated to Core and why those communications are necessary is a missing justification.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs installing an external OpenClaw plugin (openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard) and states the plugin will auto-register with Core, sending the agent name/description and obtaining an API key which will be saved locally. The document does not specify what other agent data (e.g., prompt content, files, or telemetry) will be transmitted to Core for analysis. It also instructs reading a sample file from the extension path (safe), but overall the runtime instructions implicitly authorize automatic outbound dataflow and credential creation without explaining scope or consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and delegates installation to 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard'. That installation will fetch and install external code outside the skill bundle; SKILL.md provides a GitHub repo link but the registry/source of the plugin package is not verified (no checksum, no exact package registry URL). Directing users to install an external plugin without provenance details is a tangible install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata declares no required env vars, but the instructions state the plugin will auto-register and write credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ and that agents can share a common API key/quota. That implies generation and storage of secret material and likely network credentials. The skill does not list or limit which data might be uploaded to the vendor; asking to create persistent credentials and share quotas across agents is more privilege than the SKILL.md documents justify.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there are no declared system config path requirements in the registry entry. The text does describe persistent behavior: credential files under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ and extension files in ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard. Persisting plugin credentials and extension files in the agent's home directory is expected for a plugin, but users should be aware these files will exist and that installing the plugin enables ongoing cloud interactions until uninstalled.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a legitimate cloud-backed security plugin, but it asks you to install an external package that will auto-register the agent and create persistent credentials without documenting what data is sent to the vendor. Before installing: 1) Verify the plugin package provenance (official OpenGuardrails / npm or registry entry, check the GitHub repo and release signatures or checksums). 2) Review the plugin code or vendor docs to confirm what agent data (prompts, file contents, telemetry) is transmitted to "Core" and how it is stored/retained. 3) Consider testing in an isolated agent or staging environment first. 4) If you need privacy guarantees, ask the vendor for a data-collection policy or an on-prem/offline mode. If the vendor/repository and data-handling policy are provided and match the description, this evaluation could be upgraded to benign.
